structured.approach: I followed the FE-01 procedure in the frontend-steps skill. From feat.tasks I found the Frontend lane's single task, TSK-07, which is in ap_portal. I took the stack, CI command and branch rules from org.engineering_stack. The hook (G9) does not allow shell commands in FE-01, so I checked access using the step's tool view (tool:repo-access) and read-only Reads of every repository file I cite: .git/HEAD, the feature/story reflog, ci.mjs, package.json, CLAUDE.md, src/ap_portal/index.js and tests/portal.test.js. I rewrote task.repo_access.md in full and kept the tool-result section the spine had recorded in the file. I did not push, merge or run CI.

claims.text: The Frontend lane owns TSK-07 (STORY-07, render the overdue risk table) in the ap_portal repository.
The ap_portal repository is available locally and the agent identity has write access; the git working tree is clean.
The checked-out branch is feature/story, created from dev at commit ff761ee.
No repository has to be created, and ap_portal uses no Databricks workspace or database.
ap_portal is Node.js 22 with node:test, its CI command is node ci.mjs, and CI enforces line coverage of at least 90%.
The CI static checks reject lines matching console.log or eval( and lines longer than 140 characters.
The current ap_portal version is 2.3.0, set in both src/ap_portal/index.js (VERSION) and package.json.
index.js currently exports VERSION, LABELS, formatAmount and renderAgingSummary, and TSK-07 must keep LABELS, formatAmount and renderAgingSummary unchanged.
TSK-07 may change src/ap_portal/index.js, package.json (version only) and tests/portal.test.js, and all three files already exist.
Commit messages must start with the story ID.

open_questions: RAQ-1 (non-blocking): feat.tasks and the repository's CLAUDE.md give the branch pattern feature/<story>, but the branch provided is feature/story rather than feature/STORY-07. Interim: work on feature/story as provided and put STORY-07 in commit messages. Owner: Developer.
structured.summary: FE-01 is done. The ap_portal repository is available with write access, so nothing needs to be created and no Databricks workspace or database is involved. The checked-out branch is feature/story, created from dev at commit ff761ee, and the working tree is clean. The output, task.repo_access.md, records the CI command (node ci.mjs, at least 90% coverage plus static checks), the current version (2.3.0) and the three files TSK-07 may change. I read every repository file the output cites in this session, including src/ap_portal/index.js. One non-blocking question remains: whether to keep the branch name feature/story or switch to a story-named branch.
